title: Service Discovery Fundamentals
description: Learn the fundamentals of service discovery and why it is essential for microservices.

data.text: In a microservices world, services dynamically scale up and down, and their network addresses change constantly. Service discovery solves the problem of finding these services at runtime. Netflix, Uber, and Airbnb all rely on service discovery to manage thousands of instances.

Service discovery is the process of automatically detecting devices and services on a computer network. In microservices, it allows services to find each other without hardcoding IP addresses or hostnames. Services register themselves with a registry, and clients query the registry to find available instances.

data.title: Problems with Static Configuration
items: IP addresses change when services restart or scale
Health checks are not possible without dynamic discovery
Adding new services requires updating all clients

data.title: Real-World Example
data.text: Netflix uses Eureka for service discovery, managing tens of thousands of service instances across AWS. When a service instance fails, Eureka removes it from the registry within seconds.

data.caption: Service discovery flow
data.definition:
graph LR
    S1[Service A] -->|Registers| R[Service Registry]
    S2[Service B] -->|Registers| R
    S3[Service C] -->|Queries| R
    R -->|Returns instances| S3
    S3 -->|Calls| S1

data.title: Example: Service Registration
data.code: A service registers itself with a discovery server on startup and sends heartbeats to maintain its registration.

# Service registration example
# On startup:
POST /registry/v1/instances
{
  "serviceName": "user-service",
  "host": "10.0.1.5",
  "port": 8080,
  "healthCheckUrl": "/health",
  "metadata": { "zone": "us-east-1a" }
}

# Heartbeat every 30 seconds:
PUT /registry/v1/instances/user-service-10.0.1.5:8080/heartbeat

items.question: Do I always need a service registry?
items.answer: In Kubernetes, the built-in DNS and CoreDNS often replace the need for a separate registry. In other environments, a registry like Consul or Eureka is essential.

items.question: What happens if the registry goes down?
items.answer: Clients should cache registry data locally. Netflix Eureka is designed to be highly available, but clients can still operate with cached data if it fails.

items.question: Is service discovery the same as load balancing?
items.answer: No. Service discovery finds service instances; load balancing distributes requests across them. Often, load balancing is built on top of service discovery.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Service discovery eliminates hardcoded service addresses
Services register with a registry and clients query it
Health checks keep the registry accurate
data.takeaway: Service discovery is essential for dynamic, cloud-native microservices environments.
